# lu\_factor#

scipy.linalg.lu\_factor(a, overwrite\_a=False, check\_finite=True)(
:   Compute pivoted LU decomposition of a matrix.

    The decomposition is:

    ```
     A = P L U
    ```

    where P is a permutation matrix, L lower triangular with unit diagonal elements, and U upper triangular. [...] Returns:
    :   lu(M, N) ndarray
        :   Matrix containing U in its upper triangle, and L in its lower triangle. The unit diagonal elements of L are not stored.

        piv(K,) ndarray
        :   Pivot indices representing the permutation matrix P: row i of matrix was interchanged with row piv[i]. Of shape `(K,)`, with `K =min(M,N)`.

    See also

    `lu`
    :   gives lu factorization in more user-friendly format [...] ```
    >>> p = np. argsort(p_inv)>>> parray([1, 3, 0, 2])>>> np. allclose(A - L[p] @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True
    ```

    or alternatively:

    ```
    >>> P = np. eye(4)[p]>>> np. allclose(A - P @ L @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True
    ```

:   Compute pivoted LU decomposition of a matrix.

    The decomposition is:

    ```
     A = P L U

    where P is a permutation matrix, L lower triangular with unit diagonal elements, and U upper triangular. [...] Returns:
    :   lu(M, N) ndarray
        :   Matrix containing U in its upper triangle, and L in its lower triangle. The unit diagonal elements of L are not stored.

    See also

    :   gives lu factorization in more user-friendly format [...] ```
    >>> p = np. argsort(p_inv)>>> parray([1, 3, 0, 2])>>> np. allclose(A - L[p] @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True
    ```

    or alternatively:

    ```
    >>> P = np. eye(4)[p]>>> np. allclose(A - P @ L @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True

# lu\_factor#

scipy.linalg.lu\_factor(a, overwrite\_a=False, check\_finite=True)(
:   Compute pivoted LU decomposition of a matrix.

    The decomposition is:

    ```
     A = P L U
    ```

    where P is a permutation matrix, L lower triangular with unit diagonal elements, and U upper triangular. [...] Returns:
    :   lu(M, N) ndarray
        :   Matrix containing U in its upper triangle, and L in its lower triangle. The unit diagonal elements of L are not stored.

        piv(K,) ndarray
        :   Pivot indices representing the permutation matrix P: row i of matrix was interchanged with row piv[i]. Of shape `(K,)`, with `K =min(M,N)`.

    See also

    `lu`
    :   gives lu factorization in more user-friendly format [...] ```
    >>> p = np. argsort(p_inv)>>> parray([1, 3, 0, 2])>>> np. allclose(A - L[p] @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True
    ```

    or alternatively:

    ```
    >>> P = np. eye(4)[p]>>> np. allclose(A - P @ L @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True
    ```

:   Compute pivoted LU decomposition of a matrix.

    The decomposition is:

    ```
     A = P L U
    ```

    :   lu(M, N) ndarray

    >>> p = np. argsort(p_inv)>>> parray([1, 3, 0, 2])>>> np. allclose(A - L[p] @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True
    ```

    or alternatively:

    ```
    >>> P = np. eye(4)[p]>>> np. allclose(A - P @ L @ U, np. zeros((4, 4))) True
